pageCache.pageTitle: Jubilee Year of Hope – Larmenier & Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Jubilee Year of Hope
Taking place every 25 years, a Jubilee Year is a tradition that is recognised and respected throughout the world as being a significant part of the history of our faith. During this Jubilee Year, school communities have been invited to join together as ‘pilgrims of hope’, pledging to work together for God’s kingdom of justice, peace and love.
Jubilee Launch Assembly
Our Liturgy Leaders took centre stage in a beautiful assembly to formally launch the Jubilee Year of Hope in school. Through scripture, prayer and thoughtful reflections, they encouraged the whole school community to begin this special year with open hearts and a renewed sense of purpose. The assembly reminded us that, even in uncertain times, we are called to be Pilgrims of Hope—bringing light, kindness and faith into the world around us.
Jubilee Pledge Day
Our Jubilee Pledge Day was a powerful opportunity for pupils to reflect on our school mission, make a personal commitment to be a ‘sign of hope’ and stand in solidarity with communities experiencing poverty across the world. Through this special day, pupils pledged to take concrete actions to advance justice and harmony locally, nationally and globally.
Following a Jubilee Pledge Day-themed Celebration of the Word, each class took time to consider how they could live out the principles of Catholic Social Teaching in their daily lives. Pupils reflected on how these values could be embedded more deeply at the heart of our school community to support a long-term commitment to justice.
Each class generated thoughtful and practical ideas, which have now been brought together to form our whole school ‘Jubilee Pledge’—a united expression of our commitment to living out our faith through action.
Festival of Hope for Schools
Key Stage 2 pupils proudly represented our school at the Diocesan ‘Festival of Hope for Schools’, which took place at Westminster Cathedral. This special event was a wonderful celebration of faith, unity and hope.
Jubilee Celebration Day
This special day was rooted in Catholic Social Teaching and gave pupils the opportunity to explore its key principles through a variety of engaging and meaningful experiences.
The children enjoyed a wide range of activities, including art, craft, cross-curricular tasks and opportunities to be physically active—all designed to encourage reflection, creativity and a spirit of hope and unity.
It was also a non-uniform day, and the children came dressed in their House colours—blue, green, yellow, or red—which reflect the official ‘Pilgrims of Hope’ logo. It was a joyful sight to see pupils across the school showing their House spirit while participating enthusiastically in each activity.
A highlight for many was the celebration picnic lunch, where pupils and staff came together to share food and laughter, reinforcing the strong sense of community that underpins all we do.
It was a truly memorable day, helping to bring the themes of the Jubilee Year to life in a way that was both meaningful and fun for all involved.
Jubilee Pilgrimage to Westminster Cathedral
As part of the Jubilee Year of Hope, pupils in Years 4-6 will each take part in a special pilgrimage to Westminster Cathedral, deepening their faith and reflecting on the significance of this sacred journey:
Year 6 – Friday 14th November 2025
Year 4 – Tuesday 18th November 2025
Year 5 – Friday 5th December 2025
Jubilee Finale
The Jubilee Year of Hope will come to a close in schools on Friday 21st November, marking the end of a year filled with reflection, action and spiritual growth. On this significant day, we will come together in prayer and celebration to give thanks for the many ways our school community has lived out the call to be Pilgrims of Hope. It will be a moment to look back on our shared journey and renew our commitment to carrying the message of hope into the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Our School – Larmenier & Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Dear Parents/Carers,*
Together with the Governors and staff, I am delighted to welcome you as new members to our school family.
When your children begin school, you, as parents, become fully signed up partners in the education process. In this school, staff and parents work closely together to provide a setting that supports each child’s individual learning needs.
Our first priority is to ensure the safety and wellbeing of your children so they can grow, learn and play in an atmosphere of mutual trust. All members of staff work to establish a respectful and secure relationship with their class, in an environment where children can flourish. They use their expertise to provide an engaging and challenging curriculum which deepens children’s knowledge and understanding over time and encourages them to develop as independent and resilient learners.
Religious Education, based on the teachings of the Catholic Church, is central to the school’s mission. The children’s faith and relationship with God is nurtured through learning about the life and teachings of Jesus and exploring how we live our lives as Christians. Quality prayer and worship experiences deepen children’s spiritual growth in an age-appropriate way.
The experience and opportunities your children have at this school will prepare them to move on to the next stage of their education, with a love of learning and the confidence to embrace future challenges.
We extend a warm welcome to you all.
Miss J. McGinty, Headteacher
*Whenever parents are referred to in this document, it also means carers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education – Larmenier & Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Religious Education permeates everything we do at Larmenier & Sacred Heart. It underpins all aspects of the curriculum, school life and ethos:
‘The outcome of excellent religious education is religiously literate and consciously engaged young people who have the knowledge, understanding, and skills – appropriate to their age and capacity – to reflect spiritually, and think ethically and theologically, and who recognise the demands of religious commitment in everyday life.’
(Religious Education Directory, Bishops’ Conference of England and Wales, 2023)
The Religious Education Directory (RED), To Know You More Clearly, provides a model curriculum which is rooted in Scripture and invites pupils to ‘…encounter Our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ as the living person at the heart of their study in a way that respects their individual religious identity’ (RED, 2023). The curriculum works within six ‘Branches’, revisited and built upon each academic year, in order that pupils may progress in knowledge, skill and understanding throughout their time at Larmenier & Sacred Heart.
10% of the curriculum time each week is devoted to the study of RE. Within this time, through a range of creative learning and adaptive experiences, teachers draw upon Scripture to help pupils discover how the Word of God and traditions of the Church have meaning in their everyday lives. The values and beliefs explored in lessons are encouraged and lived out in our school community.
Pupils also engage in ‘encounter and dialogue’, having the opportunity to research and learn about a range of world faiths each academic year. They learn about how believers live out their lives, how prayer has a place in the lives of followers and about different religious celebrations and festivals. The whole school also dedicates a week to learning about world faiths to enrich this learning. Throughout their career at Larmenier & Sacred Heart, we aim to enable all pupils ‘…to be confident and secure in their own religious faith, as well as being knowledgeable and respectful of other religions’ and so play ‘…a key role in building a cohesive society.’ (Christ at the Centre, Catholic Truth Society, 2012, p.9).
The RE Curriculum
Branch 1: Creation and Covenant
‘The heavens are telling the glory of God’ (Ps 19:1).
In this branch, pupils will encounter the God who creates and calls a people. They will explore the Christian belief that all that is, comes from God, hearing the Creation accounts in Genesis, and scientific explanations of the process of Creation. They will explore the call of God and his covenants (promises) made to His people, first through Abraham and Moses, then through the narrative of the Old Testament.
Branch 2: Prophecy and Promise
‘In many and various ways, God spoke to our ancestors by the prophets’ (Heb 1:1).
The prophets speak of God reaching to his people, calling them back intoa relationship with him. In this branch, pupils will explore the Christian understanding of the teaching of the prophets as they point to the fulfillment of God’s promise in a messiah (chosen one), Jesus Christ. They will explore the expectant waiting for the Messiah through the Advent season and how this speaks to Christians today as they wait for Christ. Pupils will encounter the story of the nativity of Jesus and the mystery of the incarnation.

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Social Teaching – Larmenier & Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching (CST) is at the heart of who we are as a Catholic school community. Our faith calls us to love God and to love our neighbour in every situation, especially our sisters and brothers living in poverty. Rooted in Scripture, inspired by the wisdom of Church leaders, and shaped by the voices of people around the world, CST is our moral compass, guiding us to live out the message of Jesus in our daily lives. Following in the footsteps of Christ, we are called to make God’s justice, love and peace present in our broken world, and to bring care and compassion to those near and far.
At Larmenier & Sacred Heart, CST is not just something we talk about—it underpins our learning, our choices and the way we treat one another. Pupils are encouraged to put their faith into action and to see how their learning can help make the world a better place for all, especially the most vulnerable. To support this, we use the Caritas ‘Rooted in Love’ resources, developed in partnership with the Diocese of Westminster Education Service. It addresses the objectives relating to CST from the new Religious Education Directory, including prayer and liturgy ideas around each theme, as well as suggestions for bringing this work to life in the Catholic life and mission of the school.
Rooted in Love is split into 6 themes, one for each half term:

pageCache.pageTitle: Laudato Si’ – Larmenier & Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
This year, we celebrate 10 years since Pope Francis gifted us Laudato Si’, a bold and beautiful vision for our common home.
Pope Francis’ encyclical, Laudato Si’, is a profound invitation to everyone on the planet to care for our common home.
The encyclical discusses the damage being inflicted on the Earth by humans and calls on ‘every person living on this planet’ to make urgent changes to our lifestyles.
Watch CAFOD’s animation for children on Pope Francis’ encyclical, Laudato Si’, exploring his message about caring for the world and its people.
At Larmenier & Sacred Heart pupils have the opportunity to actively take part in a diverse range of activities that explore environmental issues, thereby are immersed in the message of Laudato Si’.

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Social Teaching in Action – Larmenier & Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
The Mission Statement is the foundation upon which the school shares its responsibilities as a Catholic community towards others on a local, national and global level. The school provides a wealth of meaningful opportunities for pupils to reflect on their responsibilities and offers opportunities for them to take action.
Harvest Festival
Each Autumn, as part of our Harvest Festival celebrations, we gather together to give praise to God for the gifts and fruits of the earth. We think about those who work and care for the land and celebrate the produce grown, giving thanks for all the good things given to us by God. We reflect on what we have and think about those who are less fortunate in our local area and all around the word.
As a school community we collect and donate non-perishable food items to our local Food Bank in Hammersmith and Fulham to support people in need who live in our local community.
The Food Bank gives three days of emergency food to individuals and families in crisis, and at the Food Bank’s cafe, they also receive a hot drink, a homemade snack, a listening ear and signposting to various organisations.
The School Council plan and lead this initiative each year.
The Passage
Our annual ‘Wear a Christmas Jumper to School Day’ is an initiative to raise money to support The Passage, a charity for the homeless based in central London. A representative visits the school each year and leads an assembly on the theme of homelessness.
Catholic Children’s Society (CCS)
During Lent, the school community raises funds to support the Catholic Children’s Society’s Lenten Appeal. The children often link their fundraising efforts to their Lenten promises and pledges, putting their faith into action and growing closer to God. Each year, the Year 3 children participate in The Good Shepherd Mass at Westminster Cathedral where they present the school’s donation. In order to boost this year’s fundraising efforts the school supported the first CCS Day whereby children came to school dressed as their favourite book character to raise money.
CAFOD
The school’s annual International Day is a fundraising initiative to support the work of CAFOD. This is an event held early in the academic year that provides an opportunity for the school to celebrate cultural diversity and welcome new families to the school community.
Child Initiated Fundraising
Pupils are actively encouraged to initiate their own fundraising projects in response to local and global issues.
Larmenier & Sacred Heart has special bond with Nazareth House, Hammersmith. Victoire Larmenier (the order’s founder) and the Sisters of Nazereth play a huge part in our school’s history.

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity Parish – Larmenier & Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Holy Trinity Parish
At Larmenier & Sacred Heart we are privileged to have such a strong and special bond with Holy Trinity Church, our school parish.
We work together as a community to nurture the spiritual lives of our children, encouraging them to grow in faith and love.
Fr. Richard Andrew (Parish Priest) and Fr. Juan Sola Garcia (School Chaplain) are frequent visitors to our school. Fr. Juan leads many of our liturgical celebrations across the year and visits classes to support the children in their learning.
As a school, we attend Mass at Holy Trinity Church regularly and the children visit the church to support their learning in Religious Education.
Fr. Juan works closely with the school to provide opportunities for children to receive the Sacrament of Reconciliation. This is an established and key part of our Advent and Lenten preparations.
Our children also have the opportunity to deepen their knowledge and experiences of our faith by participation in many parish events.
To find out more about Holy Trinity Church, including Mass times, please click the link below:

Chaplaincy Team
“Jesus is calling you to be a disciple with a mission! Go, do not be afraid, and serve.”
The role of a Pupil Chaplain is to serve as a member of the Chaplaincy Team to support the Catholic life of the school.
The Chaplaincy Team perform many duties that include:
Supporting the school in its Mission Statement.
Caritas Ambassadors
The role of a Caritas Ambassador is to work in our school and the wider community as a young leader in social action.
Caritas Ambassadors perform many duties that include:
Liturgy Leaders
The role of a Liturgy Leader is to support the school in celebrating the liturgical calendar through liturgy and prayer.
Liturgy Leaders perform many duties that include:
*Year 6 Liturgy Leaders are also members of the school Chaplaincy Team to ensure a coordinated approach.
